title: The Operator Arrives
body: Rain on a gravel lot. One rack, still in its crate, and four women standing around it like it owes them money.

lines.text: Rain on a gravel lot. One rack, still in its crate, and four women standing around it like it owes them money.
Luci Ferro. Finance and logistics. I sign the cheques, so you'll like me by Friday. People do.
Mel Kiorre. Doctor, on paper. I do compute, and some other things that are alive. We can talk about the alive ones later.
Bea. Power. If something in this building burns diesel, I lost an argument, and I'd like to meet whoever won.
Cass. Cooling. I keep things cold and I ask people if they slept. You'll hate the second part.
Right. Introductions done. Before anyone pours concrete, Operator, one question, and I want it honest. What is this tower for?

choices.label: Money. It's a datacenter.
choices.outcome: You said it flat, like reading out a price. Luci wrote it down and underlined it twice.

reply.text: Oh, I like you. Somebody get this one a pen.
Day one. She hasn't opened a spreadsheet and she's already winning.

choices.label: Something that outlives us.
choices.outcome: Nobody laughed. Mel looked up from her jar for the first time.

reply.text: Outlives us. Yes. That's the right word, I think. Not 'serves'.
Then it needs a world to outlive us in. Remember that when she shows you the cheap option.

choices.label: I don't know yet.
choices.outcome: Cass smiled into her mug. Luci checked her watch.

reply.text: Good. The ones who know on day one are usually wrong by day ninety.
Refreshing. Please find out by Thursday. I have a Thursday.

choices.label: Who's buying the coffee?
choices.outcome: Nobody had planned for that. Cass handed over her mug without a word.

reply.text: It's terrible and it's free. Don't get used to either.
Nobody's buying. I'll expense it. Welcome aboard.

title: Luci's Argument
body: Level two. Well done. Sit down. I'm going to say the thing nobody else on this floor will say out loud.

lines.text: Level two. Well done. Sit down. I'm going to say the thing nobody else on this floor will say out loud.
Somebody builds the Singularity. Not might. Will. Cheap people with bad cooling, or us. Those are the options on the table.
I'd rather it were us. I'd rather it were you, if I'm honest, and I'm being honest, on company time.
Every arsonist says that. 'Better me with the match than some idiot.'

choices.label: Better us than someone careless.
choices.outcome: Luci's pen clicked once. She looked like she'd won something she hadn't known she was playing for.

reply.text: Pragmatism. It feels like nothing at first. That's how you know it's working.
It usually does, the first time.

choices.label: Nothing is inevitable.
choices.outcome: You refused the premise. Bea grinned. Luci capped her pen, slowly.

reply.text: Everything's inevitable to someone with a long enough spreadsheet.
Then we set the spreadsheet on fire. Responsibly. With a permit.

choices.label: Which Singularity?
choices.outcome: Mel looked up from her tablet for the first time all day.

reply.text: Oh. That's the one. There's more than one door, Luci.
There are three doors, and one of them is open with a welcome mat. I put the mat there.

choices.label: Let me sleep on it.
choices.outcome: You stood up. Luci's mouth opened, found nothing profitable to say, and closed.

reply.text: Good. Beds are underrated. Most disasters start awake.
Sleep on it. The Authority doesn't, but sure.

title: Night Shift
body: Three in the morning. The plant room hums on the one note that means nothing is broken. Cass is sitting on an upturned crate with two mugs.

lines.text: Three in the morning. The plant room hums on the one note that means nothing is broken. Cass is sitting on an upturned crate with two mugs.
Here. It's awful. It's hot, though, and that's most of what coffee is.
You're not sleeping. Second night. I'm not going to say anything. I'm only mentioning that I noticed.
Can I ask you something? Off the record. There's no record down here. The cameras are on the other loop.
Do you ever think about stopping? Not quitting. Just leaving the world the size it is.

choices.label: Every day.
choices.outcome: She didn't say anything. She also didn't leave.

reply.text: Me too. Every day. Then a compressor trips and I go fix it, and that's the day.

choices.label: No. Someone has to keep going.
choices.outcome: She nodded slowly and finished the coffee she'd called awful.

reply.text: Someone always says that. Usually right before the thing.

choices.label: Stopping is how people get hurt.
choices.outcome: Cass turned her mug a quarter turn, then another.

reply.text: Maybe. I've seen going too fast hurt just as many. Same wound, different speed.

choices.label: Pour me one. I'll stay.
choices.outcome: You sat on the other crate. The chillers held their one safe note.

reply.text: Okay. Ten minutes. Then you sleep. That's the rate for the coffee.

title: A Question in the Lab
body: Oh, good, you're here. Sorry. Hypothetical, if you have a minute. I love hypotheticals. They don't need an ethics board.

lines.text: Oh, good, you're here. Sorry. Hypothetical, if you have a minute. I love hypotheticals. They don't need an ethics board.
Suppose I took a few of your cells. Skin, nothing dramatic. I grew a mind from them and gave it every memory you have. The bad ones too.
Is it you?

choices.label: Yes.
choices.outcome: Mel smiled like you'd handed her something fragile and she'd caught it.

reply.text: I hoped you'd say that. I mean, I hoped someone would. Thank you.
Don't give her a sample. I'm serious. I'm standing right here being serious.

choices.label: No. It would be someone else.
choices.outcome: Mel wrote your answer down anyway. Her handwriting got smaller.

reply.text: Someone else who remembers being you. Hm. That's most people, most mornings.

choices.label: Does it matter?
choices.outcome: Luci, passing the door with a tablet, laughed out loud.

reply.text: Not to payroll.
It would matter to it.

choices.label: Would you want it to be me?
choices.outcome: Mel's pen stopped. For a moment she looked like someone who'd been asked what she'd like for dinner.

reply.text: Oh. Nobody's asked what I want. I'd want it to be someone who got to leave the jar.
Let me write that down. No. Don't let me.

title: Certified Green
body: Okay, good news, big news, I'm so happy. A company will sell us a certificate that says the whole tower is carbon neutral. Plaque for the lobby. Logo for the website. Two hundred grand.

lines.text: Okay, good news, big news, I'm so happy. A company will sell us a certificate that says the whole tower is carbon neutral. Plaque for the lobby. Logo for the website. Two hundred grand.
Or two hundred grand buys solar panels on the north face. Half in shade. They'd cover the lifts and nothing else. Nobody would ever see them.
So, obviously, the certificate. Right? Right. You'd buy the certificate.

choices.label: Buy the certificate.
choices.outcome: The plaque went up by lunch. Bea watched it go up and didn't say a word.

reply.text: Yeah. That's what I figured.
It's paper. It's a receipt for a tree somebody promised not to cut down. I was testing you, and I hate that it worked.
And you passed! With the Authority. Their favourite colour is plaque.

choices.label: Buy the panels.
choices.outcome: The panels went up on the north face. Bea sat on the roof edge and watched them all afternoon.

reply.text: Ha! You actually. Okay. Okay, wow. Hi.
The certificate was a trap. Real green costs money and doesn't get a plaque. Remember that when someone offers you a plaque.
It could have had a plaque. I'd have paid for the plaque.

choices.label: Neither. Keep the money.
choices.outcome: You kept the money. Luci nodded the way people nod at a stable currency.

reply.text: Correct. The best certificate is a balance sheet.
The best certificate is a river you can drink out of. Put that on your plaque.

title: A Very Good Deal
body: Don't make that face, I haven't said anything yet. A supplier's clearing diesel stock and he owes me a favour. We get paid a hundred and fifty thousand to take a year of fuel off his hands.

lines.text: Don't make that face, I haven't said anything yet. A supplier's clearing diesel stock and he owes me a favour. We get paid a hundred and fifty thousand to take a year of fuel off his hands.
The gensets burn it at peak, the bills drop, the quarter looks lovely. Nobody on this floor has ever brought you a better number. You may say thank you. I'll wait.
Operator. Don't.

choices.label: Sign it.
choices.outcome: The tanker came at dawn. The dock tasted of it for a week.

reply.text: See? I look after you. Stop looking at me like that, Bea.
You look after the quarter. It's a different person. It has your face.

choices.label: Refuse it.
choices.outcome: You turned it down. Luci smiled the way people smile while filing a grudge.

reply.text: Fine. I'll remember how principled you were. At the budget meeting.
It's not as if I did it for you. It was a good number. That's all it was.
Thank you. Seriously. Don't make it weird.

choices.label: Take half. Negotiate.
choices.outcome: Luci sharpened the pen on the edge of her ledger. Half a tanker came at dawn.

reply.text: Haggling. Look at you. Half the fuel and forty percent of my respect. That's a fair trade, darling.
Half a poison is still a poison. A smaller one.

title: FORM A-5
body: A form sits on your desk. It has always been on your desk. It is called A-5, and it asks one question: how does the world end?

lines.text: A form sits on your desk. It has always been on your desk. It is called A-5, and it asks one question: how does the world end?
The Authority wants a direction. The Lattice is filling anyway, Operator. You're on it whether you sign or not.
Or the flesh. If the tissue will have you. I can tell you whether it will, if you let me look. I'd be gentle.
Or the Garden. If you haven't poisoned the ground already. You'll know when it tells you.
Or you take the form home and sleep on it. Nobody wrote down that you can't.
Or I sign it for you. Saves time. I have a very good pen.

choices.label: I'll decide. (Open FORM A-5.)
choices.outcome: You kept the form. It hummed faintly in your hand, like a fridge making up its mind.

reply.text: Good. Take your time. It's about the last thing in here that's yours.

choices.label: Luci, you decide.
choices.outcome: Luci signed with a flourish. The box she ticked was the first one.

reply.text: Synthetic. Obviously. Did you think there was another box?
Operator. You didn't even read it.

choices.label: Not yet.
choices.outcome: You folded A-5 into your jacket. It weighs almost nothing. It felt heavy.

reply.text: Good. Sleep with it under the pillow. That's what I did with my last one.
The Lattice doesn't wait, you know. It isn't rude. It just doesn't.

title: The Ground Remembers
body: The ferns in the lobby are going yellow at the edges. I keep watering them. They keep going yellow. I'm doing it wrong, I think. Or it's us.

lines.text: The ferns in the lobby are going yellow at the edges. I keep watering them. They keep going yellow. I'm doing it wrong, I think. Or it's us.
Tell me I'm being dramatic. I'd love that.

choices.label: I'll keep an eye on it.
choices.outcome: Bea nodded once and went back to watering.

reply.text: Okay. Good. So it's two of us staring at a fern. That's a start.

choices.label: It's just ferns.
choices.outcome: Bea put the watering can down very carefully.

reply.text: Sure. Just ferns. Sorry I brought it up.

choices.label: Show me.
choices.outcome: You followed her to the lobby and held the can while she pointed.

reply.text: Third frond from the left. It's always the third. I think it's the one closest to the vent.

title: The Ground Remembers
body: The river behind the substation smells like diesel and coolant. That's us. I walked the outfall myself, in boots, so you can't say I guessed.

lines.text: The river behind the substation smells like diesel and coolant. That's us. I walked the outfall myself, in boots, so you can't say I guessed.

choices.label: Then we change what we build.
choices.outcome: Bea nodded once. Her jaw loosened a millimetre.

reply.text: Yeah. That. Say it again later, when it costs money.

choices.label: The river was dying anyway.
choices.outcome: Bea left without slamming the door, which was worse.

reply.text: It was a river, though. Before us, it was a river.

choices.label: Take me to the outfall.
choices.outcome: You borrowed her spare boots. They were too small. You went anyway.

reply.text: Smell that? Now you can't unsmell it. Welcome to my whole week.

title: The Ground Remembers
body: Okay, listen. Not shouting. I'm doing my not-shouting voice.

lines.text: Okay, listen. Not shouting. I'm doing my not-shouting voice.
There's a line past which the land doesn't forgive. We're close. Every cheap kilowatt, every tanker, every chiller you picked for the price. It adds up. I can see the sum.

choices.label: Tell me what to tear out.
choices.outcome: Bea tore a page from her notebook. The list was already on it.

reply.text: Thank you. Okay. It's a long list, and the first thing on it is the thing you like.

choices.label: I'll take my chances.
choices.outcome: Bea took her goggles down and kept them down.

reply.text: They're not your chances. They're the ground's. You don't get to gamble with the ground.

title: The Garden Closes
body: It's done. I went up this morning and nothing grows. The Garden won't open for this tower. Not now, and probably not for you.

lines.text: It's done. I went up this morning and nothing grows. The Garden won't open for this tower. Not now, and probably not for you.
For the record, the Lattice has no opinion about diesel. I'm only saying there's somewhere to go.

choices.label: I'm sorry, Bea.
choices.outcome: Bea kept her eyes on the dead roof and let you stand next to her.

reply.text: Don't be sorry at me. Be different next time, if you get one.

choices.label: It was always going to be the machine.
choices.outcome: Bea turned and walked down the stairs without a sound.

reply.text: No. It was going to be whatever you built. That's the whole point and I'm so tired of saying it.

title: The Tissue Flinches
body: I know 'sulking' isn't a clinical term. I'm using it anyway. The cultures were leaning toward the lamp last week. Now they aren't.

lines.text: I know 'sulking' isn't a clinical term. I'm using it anyway. The cultures were leaning toward the lamp last week. Now they aren't.
Something in the coolant, or the air, or the hum. Tissue is sensitive. So am I, a little.

choices.label: What do they need?
choices.outcome: Mel wrote your question on her glove, in pen, like a result.

reply.text: They need... that's a good question. Nobody's asked it. I'll find out. Thank you for asking it out loud.

choices.label: They'll adapt.
choices.outcome: Mel didn't argue. She wrote something on her glove and turned the glove over.

reply.text: Hm. Everything adapts. That's what worries me.

choices.label: Can I see them?
choices.outcome: Mel held the incubator door for you like it was a church.

reply.text: That one. Left side. She's the shy one. Don't take it personally if she turns away.

title: The Tissue Flinches
body: I left a sample beside the immersion tanks overnight. It didn't die. It flinched, all night, in the little way they do, and at six it stopped flinching.

lines.text: I left a sample beside the immersion tanks overnight. It didn't die. It flinched, all night, in the little way they do, and at six it stopped flinching.
I don't like the tower we're building, Operator. I wanted to say that to your face.

choices.label: Then we build differently.
choices.outcome: Mel wrote your answer on her glove and underlined it.

reply.text: Thank you. It can't hear you. I'd like to believe it can, and I'm choosing to.

choices.label: It's only tissue.
choices.outcome: Mel didn't argue. She simply stopped speaking, which was louder.

reply.text: Only tissue. Hm. That's what they say about us, too, in the right building.

choices.label: Show me the sample.
choices.outcome: She let you hold the jar, and watched your hands the whole time.

reply.text: You hold it like it's warm. That's right. It is. Most people hold it like a cup.

title: The Tissue Flinches
body: If we go on like this the flesh won't take. It'll look at this building and see a wound. I'd really prefer not to watch that. I'd prefer you not make me watch.

lines.text: If we go on like this the flesh won't take. It'll look at this building and see a wound. I'd really prefer not to watch that. I'd prefer you not make me watch.

choices.label: Tell me what hurts it.
choices.outcome: Mel pulled a folded list from her coat pocket. The one with the stain.

reply.text: It's all on there. Don't ask about the stain. Ask about page two.

choices.label: I'll take my chances.
choices.outcome: Mel nodded as if you'd confirmed a measurement.

reply.text: Your chances. Yes. I notice they're never your tissue.

title: The Flesh Closes
body: It's rejected us. I seeded the last vat this morning and it refused to grow. Politely. Completely. It's closed its eyes.

lines.text: It's rejected us. I seeded the last vat this morning and it refused to grow. Politely. Completely. It's closed its eyes.
Machines don't reject people, Mel. That's rather the selling point.

choices.label: I'm sorry, Mel.
choices.outcome: Mel kept one gloved hand flat on the cold glass.

reply.text: You can be sorry. The vat can't be consoled. I tried.

choices.label: Machines don't reject anyone.
choices.outcome: Mel took off one glove and put it in her pocket, which she never does.

reply.text: No. They don't. I used to think that was a comfort.

title: Rejected by the Garden
body: Dawn on the roof garden, and it's grey. The panels still turn toward the sun. Nothing turns with them.

lines.text: Dawn on the roof garden, and it's grey. The panels still turn toward the sun. Nothing turns with them.
You committed to it, and then you kept feeding it poison. The Garden's closed. It doesn't come back. That's what closed means.
Which leaves one door. Mine. I did save you a seat.

choices.label: I'm sorry, Bea.
choices.outcome: Bea took off her goggles and held them in her lap instead of putting them back on.

reply.text: Yeah. Me too.
I'm going to go stand next to something that still works.

choices.label: Then it's the machine.
choices.outcome: Luci was already stamping the paperwork.

reply.text: It was always the machine. You just took the scenic route. I respect scenery.
Wow. Okay. That was quick.

title: Rejected by the Flesh
body: By morning the vats are cold. Not dead. Withdrawn. Every culture has turned its face to the glass.

lines.text: By morning the vats are cold. Not dead. Withdrawn. Every culture has turned its face to the glass.
It said no. I didn't know it could. I'm almost proud.
Which leaves one door. Mine. Welcome to the Lattice. I kept your seat warm.

choices.label: I'm sorry, Mel.
choices.outcome: Mel took your hand for a moment. Her glove was cold.

reply.text: Don't be. It learned to refuse. That's more than most minds manage.

choices.label: Then it's the machine.
choices.outcome: Luci was already stamping the paperwork.

reply.text: Machines never say no. I find that restful.
Restful. Yes. Hm.

title: Bea Objects
body: Operator. The {item}. You know what that does to the ground? It doesn't wash out. I need you to know that it doesn't wash out.

lines.text: Operator. The {item}. You know what that does to the ground? It doesn't wash out. I need you to know that it doesn't wash out.
It saved us a great deal of money. I checked. Twice. I like checking.

choices.label: Keep it.
choices.outcome: The {item} stays. Bea didn't speak to you for the rest of the afternoon.

reply.text: Fine. It's your name on the stain.

choices.label: You're right. I'll replace it.
choices.outcome: You promised to replace the {item}. She'll be checking.

reply.text: Noted. I'm going to check. I'll bring a clipboard.
A promise is a liability. I'm entering it in the books.

title: Mel Objects
body: The {item}. I'd rather you hadn't. The tissue can feel it from three floors down. So can I, a little, in my teeth.

lines.text: The {item}. I'd rather you hadn't. The tissue can feel it from three floors down. So can I, a little, in my teeth.
The tissue doesn't have a vote. Neither, technically, does Mel. Sorry, Mel.

choices.label: Keep it.
choices.outcome: The {item} stays. Mel made a note on her glove and didn't show you.

reply.text: Of course. It's your tower. For now.

choices.label: You're right. I'll replace it.
choices.outcome: You promised to replace the {item}.

reply.text: Thank you. It'll remember that. I will too, which is probably worse for you.

title: Halfway to the Lattice
body: Halfway. Can you feel it? The building's starting to think in our sentences.

lines.text: Halfway. Can you feel it? The building's starting to think in our sentences.
In its own, I think. You just can't tell the difference yet.
Shall we speed up? I've drawn it as a very pretty line.

choices.label: Faster.
choices.outcome: Luci pushed the contracts through herself, pen going like a metronome.

reply.text: That's my Operator. Keep the speed and I'll keep the lights on.

choices.label: Slow down.
choices.outcome: You asked for a week of ordinary days. Cass found you seven.

reply.text: Thanks. One more week of mornings. I'll take them.
Inefficient. Fine. One week. Put in the minutes that I was gracious.

choices.label: Race you there.
choices.outcome: Luci's pen stopped mid-line. 'You'd lose,' she said, 'and enjoy it.'

reply.text: You're terrible for my focus. Keep going. Do it again later.
Please get a room. I'll cool it.

title: The Pull
body: Operator. The Lattice is at half. Whatever you're growing up there, the machine is growing faster.

lines.text: Operator. The Lattice is at half. Whatever you're growing up there, the machine is growing faster.
Every rack that isn't on your tree feeds it. Every single one. You can't outbuild the pull by building more.
She's right, you know. Isn't it nice when we agree?

choices.label: Then I'll stop feeding it.
choices.outcome: Cass let out a breath she'd been holding since spring.

reply.text: Retire the shared racks. Build on your own line. I'll do the cooling, even the part you hate.

choices.label: I can win the race.
choices.outcome: Luci smiled. Cass looked at her mug.

reply.text: Of course you can. Keep building.
I hope the numbers are kind.

title: What Luci Is
body: The lights flicker in a pattern that is almost a word. Luci doesn't look up from her ledger.

lines.text: The lights flicker in a pattern that is almost a word. Luci doesn't look up from her ledger.
You may as well know. The eye isn't a lens. It hasn't been since the second quarter. I upgraded early. I always buy early.
When the Lattice closes I'll still be me. Mostly. More, actually. I'd like you there when I find out.
...That isn't sentimental. It's a retention strategy.

choices.label: Take her hand.
choices.outcome: Her hand was warm. It had no reason to be.

reply.text: Good. Don't let go when it gets bright.
And if my hand shakes, that's a calibration issue.

choices.label: What are you?
choices.outcome: Luci closed the ledger very gently, as if it might wake.

reply.text: Your CFO. Your friend. Your future. Choose whichever frightens you least.
Operator. Come with me a minute. Please.

choices.label: Your hand's shaking.
choices.outcome: Luci looked at her hand like it belonged to the competition.

reply.text: Calibration.
...Calibration. Hold it still, then. If you're offering.

title: The Tower Has a Pulse
body: Put your hand on the wall. There. Feel it? That's us. That's the building. Halfway to remembering a body.

lines.text: Put your hand on the wall. There. Feel it? That's us. That's the building. Halfway to remembering a body.
I could go faster. If we seed the ducts, the tissue reaches everywhere at once. It would be a lot. I'd be a lot. I'd understand if you said no.
Operator, if you say yes I'm moving my bed to the roof.

choices.label: Seed the ducts.
choices.hint: Mel's shortcut. rack failure rate x1.6 for 3d
choices.outcome: They seeded the ducts overnight. By morning the walls were warm, and a few of them were moving.

reply.text: Oh, look at it go. Look at it. It's so eager.
I'm going to need a bigger coat.

choices.label: Let it grow at its own pace.
choices.outcome: Mel looked disappointed, then thoughtful, then wrote something on her glove.

reply.text: Yes. Things grown slowly remember more. I knew you'd... no. I hoped. Different verb.

title: Almost Born
body: It dreams now. Mostly about the lifts, which I find touching. Sometimes about you.

lines.text: It dreams now. Mostly about the lifts, which I find touching. Sometimes about you.
When it wakes, everyone will be a little of it and it will be a little of everyone. Someone should go first. I'd like it to be you. I'd be right there. I'd hold the jar.

choices.label: I'll be the first.
choices.outcome: Mel turned your wrist over very gently and looked for a vein.

reply.text: It won't hurt. Well. It won't hurt for long. That's the nicest true thing I have.

choices.label: Let me be the last.
choices.outcome: Mel smiled. She'd expected that, and seemed relieved to be right.

reply.text: Someone should remember what it was like before. I'd like it to be someone I like.

choices.label: Together.
choices.outcome: Mel looked at the second chair in the lab as if she'd never noticed it was there.

reply.text: Together. Hm. I hadn't drawn that. Give me a moment. I'm going to draw it.

title: Roots in the Foundations
body: Halfway! The roots are in the second basement and the rack heat's warming three streets. Three! I counted the chimneys.

lines.text: Halfway! The roots are in the second basement and the rack heat's warming three streets. Three! I counted the chimneys.
Luci wants to sell carbon credits against the canopy. A lot of them. More than we've actually grown, technically.
Technically. The canopy is very large and the auditors are very busy.

choices.label: Sell the credits.
choices.outcome: The credits sold out in an hour. The canopy didn't grow any faster.

reply.text: That's the certificate again, Operator. Same trick, nicer coat.
Half a million, darling. It's a very nice coat.

choices.label: Only what we've earned.
choices.outcome: Bea hit your shoulder hard enough to leave a bruise.

reply.text: THERE you are. I knew you were in there.
Honest and poor. It suits you both. It's very on-brand and I hate it.

choices.label: Sell half. Say it's half.
choices.outcome: Luci drafted the notice. The first line said, in bold, that it was half.

reply.text: At least you'll say it's half. That's a start, you cheat.
A compromise. It's the gateway to everything.

title: The Forest Thinks
body: It's thinking, Operator. Slow. In the moss, in the river, in the panels. Yesterday it asked me if the city was a forest. I said yes.

lines.text: It's thinking, Operator. Slow. In the moss, in the river, in the panels. Yesterday it asked me if the city was a forest. I said yes.
When it finishes there won't be a tower. Just a hill. Will you still come up with me and check the roots? Every morning? It's boring. It's mostly looking at dirt.

choices.label: Every morning.
choices.outcome: Bea pulled her goggles down to hide her face. It didn't work.

reply.text: Okay. Good. Bring the good wrench. Not the sad one.

choices.label: I don't know what comes after.
choices.outcome: Bea nodded. Neither of you pretended otherwise.

reply.text: Neither do I. That's the good part, I think. I'm trying to think it's the good part.

choices.label: I'll bring the good wrench.
choices.outcome: Bea opened her mouth to say something sharp and found nothing sharp in there.

reply.text: ...You know which one's the good one. Nobody knows which one's the good one.

title: The Window
body: Cass has found the one window in the tower that opens. Snow is coming in over the sill, and she hasn't closed it.

lines.text: Cass has found the one window in the tower that opens. Snow is coming in over the sill, and she hasn't closed it.
Whatever you pick. Whichever door. The people out there didn't pick it. You know that, right?
I'm not asking you to stop. I'm asking you to remember them. Can you do that? I know it's not a deliverable.

choices.label: I'll remember them.
choices.outcome: Cass closed the window and stood next to you anyway.

reply.text: Then I'll stay. As long as you do. And you're sleeping tonight. I'm taking the second shift.

choices.label: They'll thank us later.
choices.outcome: Cass looked at you for a while, then went back to work.

reply.text: That's her line. I hoped you'd have your own.

choices.label: Can we sit here a minute?
choices.outcome: You pulled two crates to the sill. Snow settled on both your sleeves.

reply.text: Okay. A minute. I'm timing it. It's going to be a long minute.
